<h1 id="Blaney%E2%80%93Criddle-(1950)-Temperature-Based-PET">Blaney–Criddle (1950) Temperature-Based PET<a class="anchor-link" href="#Blaney%E2%80%93Criddle-(1950)-Temperature-Based-PET">¶</a></h1><p><strong>Experiment 049</strong> — Python control baseline aligned with primal <code>science.et0_blaney_criddle</code> and Rust <code>validate_blaney_criddle</code>.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="cell border-box-sizing text_cell rendered"><div class="inner_cell">
<div class="text_cell_render border-box-sizing rendered_html">
<h2 id="Theory">Theory<a class="anchor-link" href="#Theory">¶</a></h2><p>The original Blaney–Criddle relation estimates consumptive use / PET from mean monthly temperature and the <strong>mean daily fraction of annual daytime hours</strong> $p$ (latitude and month).</p>
<p>$$\mathrm{ET}_0 = p \, (0.46\, T + 8.13) \quad [\mathrm{mm\,day}^{-1}]$$</p>
<p>with $T$ mean monthly temperature (°C) and $p$ as a 0–1 fraction (SCS-TP-96; FAO-24 Table 18 for tabulated $p$). FAO-24 humidity and wind corrections are <strong>not</strong> applied here — this matches the western-US irrigation form in the control script.</p>
<p><strong>Citation:</strong> Blaney HF, Criddle WD (1950) <em>Determining water requirements in irrigated areas from climatological and irrigation data</em>. USDA-SCS Technical Paper 96.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
